text: Decided to keep the Juniper Street Tech Hub open Saturdays 10-2 instead of Friday evenings; Friday turnout was 3 people on average, Saturday pilots drew 14.
Plan for spring: two laptop-repair nights a month, one 'phone basics' class for seniors, and a sign-up sheet at the library desk.
Chose to apply for the county Digital Inclusion mini-grant ($8,000) rather than the state one; the state application needs audited financials we don't have yet.
County mini-grant portal rejected our PDF budget twice (file over 5 MB). Fixed by exporting at 150 dpi; submitted on March 29.
Volunteer roster: Priya (repairs, Tuesdays), Marcus (seniors class), Dee (front desk, Saturdays). Priya prefers texts over email.
Seniors learn faster with printed one-page guides than with slides. Keep font at 18pt minimum.
Promised the county we'd report quarterly: first report due July 15, then October 15 and January 15.
Two donated laptops had failing SSDs. Rule going forward: run a SMART check before accepting any donated machine.
Physical therapy twice a week through June for the knee; no lifting over 20 lb at the hub until cleared.
Switched the sign-up sheet from paper to a simple web form; paper stays as a backup at the desk.
Planted tomatoes and basil in the hub's side bed with the Saturday group; Marcus built the trellis.
County grant awarded: $8,000, restricted to devices, hotspots and class materials. No staff wages from this money.
Decided to hire a part-time coordinator in the fall, funded from general donations (the county grant can't pay wages).
Filed the first quarterly report to the county one day early, with class counts (41 attendees) and 12 devices distributed.
The Saturday web form double-booked the 11am slot twice. Workaround: cap each slot at 4 and send a confirmation text.
Reversed the July decision: no coordinator hire this fall. Donations came in 40% under plan; revisit in January.
Mom's birthday is September 21. Book the Thai place for Sunday the 20th, 6 people.
Hotspot lending works best with a one-week loan and a text reminder on day 6; returns went from 60% to 95%.
Next county report due October 15: need device counts, class attendance since July, and two participant quotes.
Priya can't do Tuesdays in October; Dee offered to cover the first two repair nights.
Cleared by the PT for normal lifting. Can move the donated monitors again.
Idea for winter: a 'scam spotting' class with the library, since three seniors got fake 'package delivery' texts this month.
County contact for the grant is the Digital Inclusion desk; reports go through the same portal as the application (watch the 5 MB limit).
Agreed with the library to co-host the scam-spotting class on November 7, 10am, in their community room.
